known_worker_asymmetry: The supervisor version's workers use re.search (first ID in the whole conversation history); the workflow version's use re.findall (every ID in one isolated task string). That is a worker-level difference as well as a routing one, so questions with two IDs for one worker are reported but flagged.
corrections: v1.2, after the first run and before reporting: added wording to the scorer's not-found phrase list (hard-03, hard-04 were correct refusals the checker misread), relaxed hardturn-04's fact label, and stopped scoring hard-14 on a field neither version's SQL returns. All three apply to both systems equally. Results before and after the correction are both recorded.

v1.3: edge-05 was labelled to expect a refusal because the README says lowercase IDs are not recognised. The current version answers it correctly, because the planner normalises the ID when it writes the task. The label encoded my prediction rather than the correct answer, so it was changed to check the correct answer. This one favours the current version and is called out for that reason.
